column1: # tests/expected-errno.tsv — the canonical per-case expected result for
# tests/rkvenc-invalid-ioctl.c.
# WHY THE TABLE IS DATA AND NOT A SWITCH STATEMENT. The harness and the kernel
# change together, and a harness that carries its own expectations inline can be
# "fixed" to agree with whatever the driver now does. Keeping the expectations in
# a reviewed file means changing what a malformed request returns is a visible
# diff in this table, and the host fixture validates the table BEFORE it is ever
# copied to a board — so a duplicate, unknown, missing or malformed row fails on
# the workstation rather than being discovered mid-drill.
# Columns, tab-separated:
#   case      the --case name the harness accepts, unique, [a-z0-9-]+
#   errno     the expected errno NAME, or OK for a request that must succeed
#   what      what the request is malformed in (one line, human)
# EINVAL means the driver rejected the shape. EFAULT means it rejected the
# buffer. ENOMEM is reserved for the injected allocation failure — a malformed
# request must NEVER produce it, which is exactly what the old code did by
# collapsing every rkvenc_alloc_task() failure into a bare NULL.
